events.title: Asian Shares Mixed As AI Profit Concerns Weigh
events.description: Asian shares ended mixed on Tuesday as tech and AI-related shares remained shacky and oil prices rebounded on heightened fears of Middle East escalation.

events.title: NZ Dollar Slides Against Most Majors
events.description: The New Zealand dollar weakened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Tuesday.

events.title: Australian Dollar Falls Against Majors
events.description: The Australian dollar weakened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Tuesday.

events.title: European Shares Set To Open Lower As Trump's Second Term Faces Crucial Test
events.description: European stocks may open on a sluggish note on Tuesday after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reversed early gains to end lower overnight on growing pessimism about big tech and the artificial intelligence trade.

events.title: Indian Shares Climb For Fourth Day
events.description: Indian shares opened on a buoyant note on Tuesday, extending gains for a fourth consecutive session as Brent oil prices slumped to $105 a barrel amid hopes of a de-escalation in the Middle East conflict.

events.title: Australian Market Trims Early Gains In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian stock market is trimming its early gains in mid-market trading on Tuesday, reversing some of the losses in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is staying above the 8,850 level, with gains in gold mining and technology stocks partially offset by weakness in energy and financial stocks.

events.title: Asian Markets Trade Mostly Lower
events.description: Asian markets are mostly lower on Tuesday, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight, as South Korean markets tumbled amid weakness in semiconductor stocks on concerns over returns on huge AI spending and mixed earnings and cautious forecasts from major US technology firms. Meanwhile, reports suggesting a possible de-escalation in the Middle East sent crude oil price tumbling.

events.title: Indian Shares Set To Extend Gains As Oil Prices Slump On US-Iran Peace Hopes
events.description: Indian shares look set to open higher on Tuesday, adding to recent gains as crude oil prices continued to ease amid hopes of a de-escalation in the Middle East conflict.

events.title: Thai Stock Market Due For Support On Tuesday
events.description: The Thai stock market has finished lower in five straight sessions, sliding more than 70 points or 4.4 percent in that span. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just beneath the 1,510-point plateau although it may stop the bleeding on Tuesday.

events.title: Indonesia Stock Market May Remain Rangebound On Tuesday
events.description: The Indonesia stock market on Monday ended the two-day losing streak in which it had dropped more than 225 points or 4 percent. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just beneath the 5,100-point plateau and it's expected to see little movement on Tuesday.

events.title: Rally May Stall For Hong Kong Stock Market
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has moved higher in two straight sessions, collecting more than 430 points or 1.9 percent along the way. The Hang Seng now sits just beneath the 23,400-point plateau although it may run out of steam on Tuesday.

events.title: China Stock Market May Hand Back Monday's Gains
events.description: The China stock market on Monday snapped the two-day losing streak in which it had dropped more than 80 points or 2.2 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,640-point plateau although it may remain stuck in neutral on Tuesday.

events.title: Australian Markets Modestly Higher
events.description: The Australian stock market is modestly higher on Tuesday, reversing the losses in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving well above the 8,850 level, with gains across most sectors led by mining and technology stocks. Energy stocks were the only weak spot on tumbling crude oil prices.
